description: Answers "were there magnetic storms yesterday / this week / this month?", "what was the strongest storm lately?". What the planetary K index did over the last 24 hours (hourly peaks of the NOAA estimate), 7 days (three-hourly values) or 30 days (daily peaks), in the asker's time zone, with the maximum and how many values reached a storm. Gaps are null, not zero. Geophysical data only; no health information.

period.description: 24h: hourly peaks; 7d: three-hourly values; 30d: daily peaks. Defaults to 24h. The service keeps 30 days.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the person asking, such as Europe/Moscow or America/New_York. Local times and days use it. Defaults to UTC.

name: get_kp_history

level.description: NOAA G-scale level. Kp is graded by the whole number it rounds to, so 4.67 is already G1.

max.description: The highest value of the period and when.

missingCount.description: How many of the values have nothing measured.

sources.description: Where the data comes from and on what terms.

stormCount.description: How many of the values reached a storm, G1 or above.

date.description: For daily values: the local calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD.

start.description: Start of the hour, interval or day, UTC.

startLocal.description: The same in the requested time zone.

level.description: NOAA G-scale level. Kp is graded by the whole number it rounds to, so 4.67 is already G1.

value.description: Null when nothing was measured: a gap, not a quiet field.

title: Kp history
